content:
Director of National Intelligence Jay Clayton said recent tech outages across the country are “unrelated.”

Clayton opened Wednesday’s testimony to Congress by attempting to downplay the outages, which hit the Federal Aviation Administration, the National Security Agency, banks and major tech companies.

“I want to briefly address cyber threats,” Clayton said. “Before I do that, I want to address the several unrelated issues that have recently caused service disruptions. I understand the timing of these incidents can raise questions, and it should ― the American people should ask us these questions. But based on what we know today, after a great deal of diligence, these are separate service outages associated with maintenance and technical changes. They are not a coordinated or state-sponsored attack.”

The timing of the outages ― all within the last week ― has raised eyebrows that they could be related. Rep. Dan Goldman (D-N.Y.) pressed Clayton on the issue later in his testimony.

“Is it your testimony today that the American people should believe that the series and sequence of events in the last week is purely coincidental?” Goldman asked.

“We have no indication that these events are related,” Clayton said.

Not all lawmakers are convinced.

“You know, the four biggest banks in America, the major airlines, the entire air traffic control system, the NSA, all within days of each other,” Sen. Josh Hawley (R-Mo.) told HuffPost on Tuesday. “I mean, that is quite a coincidence.”

“The government’s telling us everything’s fine,” Watters said on his show Monday. “Is it? It doesn’t seem like it.”
